title: The asset has an Inspections tab that lists every inspection
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in with 'Customers - View' and 'Work orders - View', on the build under test.
  2. An asset reachable from a customer record, with several inspections including repeated runs of the same template. Seed: run several inspections on one asset (some from the same template) and complete them.
custom_steps:
1. Open the asset record and confirm an Inspections tab appears alongside Work Orders, Invoices and Notes.
2. Confirm the tab lists every inspection linked to the asset, most recently completed first.
3. Read a row's columns: inspection, status, completion date, technician who signed, findings, work order, report, and an action.
4. Confirm the inspection column shows the template name with its version beneath.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • An Inspections tab appears on the asset record, alongside Work Orders, Invoices and Notes.
  • The tab lists every inspection linked to that asset, most recently completed first.
  • Each row shows the inspection, its status, the completion date, the technician who signed it, the findings, the work order it was run on, the report, and an action.
  • The inspection column shows the template name with its version beneath, which distinguishes repeated runs of the same template.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-8181, story SV-9103 (S5 — Inspection history on the asset record); Digital Inspections V2 specification, Confluence page 768507905, section S5; read on 22 September 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S5-R1: “An Inspections tab will appear on the asset record, alongside Work Orders, Invoices and Notes”
  • S5-R2: “The tab will list every inspection linked to that asset, most recently completed first”
  • S5-R3: “Each row will show the inspection, its status, the completion date, the technician who signed it, the findings, the work order it was run on, the report, and an action”
  • S5-R4: “The inspection column will show the template name with its version beneath, which is what distinguishes repeated runs of the same template”

Last checked against build v26.36.8-2a64085 on 10/1/2026.
